title: Audit and remediate transitive crypto vectors in third-party SSO adapters
creator: Priya Nair
description: Perform a focused audit of transitive cryptographic dependency vectors pulled in by SSO/SSO-adapter libraries (SAML, OIDC, JWT helpers), remediate vulnerable call sites, and standardize a lightweight crypto shim to reduce attack surface. This ticket targets both direct and transitive dependencies that introduce vulnerable OpenSSL or XML/JWT parsing code paths and documents a safe upgrade path for runtime packages.
background: Recent dependency scans surfaced multiple transitive CVE candidates coming from legacy SSO adapters and JWT helper packages used across the control plane and private agent. We observed inconsistent use of verified JWT libraries (some services using unmaintained forks) and xmlsec bindings with mixed OpenSSL linkage. Left unaddressed, these vectors could allow signature bypass or parser-induced DoS under crafted input.
goals: 1) Inventory affected services and adapter versions; 2) Replace or patch vulnerable transitive libs; 3) Introduce a vetted crypto shim and enforce it via linter/CI banlist; 4) Add integration tests that simulate malformed SAML/JWT artifacts; 5) Complete security review and roll out to staging then prod.
out_of_scope: Full migration to a different SSO provider or rearchitecting auth flow. This ticket focuses on dependency remediation, small adapter patches, and rollout safety mechanisms.
acceptance_criteria: - All services depending on vulnerable transitive packages listed in the inventory have either an upgraded dependency or an applied mitigation.
acceptance_criteria_2: - A minimal crypto shim (signature verification + safe XML parsing wrappers) is merged and adopted by at least 80% of SSO callsites in the control plane.
acceptance_criteria_3: - CI linter rejects any new deps that match the banned CVE patterns and a docs page details the approved library list.
tasks: 1) Run exhaustive SBOM + dependency-graph scan (OWASP-DependencyCheck + internal tooling). 2) Triage CVE candidates and map to callsites. 3) Prototype crypto shim with clear API for verify_jwt, verify_saml_signature, parse_safe_xml. 4) Implement adapter patches or replace libraries. 5) Add integration tests + fuzz harness for XML/JWT parsing. 6) Rollout: canary to staging -> infra e2e -> prod with monitoring. 7) Post-rollout security sign-off.
implementation_notes: Prefer using maintained JOSE/JWT libraries (no unmaintained forks). For XML parsing use a streaming, non-DTD parser and bind xmlsec only with FIPS-compatible OpenSSL where available. Keep shim minimal: no new crypto primitives; delegate to platform KMS for critical operations. Ensure transitive OpenSSL upgrades are verified at the binary link level (ldd / otool), and add a smoke test that asserts expected OpenSSL version at startup.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: staging canary on control-plane replicas (10%) with increased SSO logging. Phase 2: staged rollout across private agents with feature flag to switch to shim. Phase 3: full cutoff of old adapter path and monitor for error spike for 72 hours. If errors > 0.5% relative increase trigger automatic rollback.
testing_plan: Unit tests for shim API, integration tests with known-good and malformed SAML/JWT artifacts, mutation tests for XML parser, and a CI gating job that re-scans dependency tree on PR. Add a nightly fuzz job targeting XML/JWT parsing harness.
risks:
- Upgrading OpenSSL/transitive libs may change binary ABI affecting on-prem agents.
- Behavioral differences in JWT libraries (clock skew handling) may cause token validation failures.
- Aggressive parser hardening could break integrations with legacy partner IdPs.
mitigation:
- Build and smoke-test agent images against matrix of OS versions.
- Add a compatibility mode toggle that preserves previous validation semantics for 2 weeks while monitoring.
- Coordinate partner outreach for IdP compatibility where needed.
notes: Initial SBOM scan completed 2025-02-20. Found three high-confidence transitive OpenSSL linkages coming from xmlsec-java bindings in legacy SSO-adapter v0.9.x and an unmaintained jwt-helper fork. Prioritized xmlsec bindings because they link directly to system OpenSSL and are reachable from control-plane login flow. Security team flagged the jwt-helper as 'requires replacement'.
